title: Make MergeStore.upsert + persistUpdatedAt atomic to stop a stale LWW shadow-timestamp surviving a mid-merge crash
rule: DB-2 (>1 write runs inside a single transaction()) / Nygard: process death mid-write

why: Every natural-key LWW merger applies the remote row (_store.upsert, which writes the entity table including its own updatedAt column) and THEN separately persists the SyncKv shadow timestamp (_store.persistUpdatedAt) as two independent awaited Drift writes with no enclosing db.transaction(). If the process dies between the two — an OS kill or force-quit on mobile is routine, not exotic — the entity row is left holding the remote's updatedAt while SyncKv still holds the pre-merge value. Any local edit made before the next successful sync now races a STALE local timestamp: a re-pulled, unchanged remote row will look newer than the stale SyncKv record and DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer will silently let it overwrite the user's genuinely-newer local edit — no exception, no log, nothing to retry against. This is DB-2's 'crash mid-sequence leaves the DB half-written' failure applied to the LWW bookkeeping itself.
recommendation: Add a MergeStore.applyRemote(...) that wraps the entity write and its SyncKv persistUpdatedAt in one db.transaction() (or expose a transaction-scoped variant), and switch all 8 callers to it.
acceptance_criteria: Fault-injection/unit test: call upsert() alone (simulating a crash before persistUpdatedAt commits), then perform a legitimately-newer local edit to the same row, then re-merge the identical stale remote row — assert the local edit survives.
New transaction-wrapped MergeStore method has a unit test asserting both writes roll back together when the second write is forced to fail.

corrections: 3 of the 8 sites (bookmark_merger.dart, goal_merger.dart, learning_order_merger.dart) have a redundant per-DAO LWW guard (e.g. BookmarkDao.upsertBookmarkByProfile checks `updatedAt.isAfter(existing.updatedAt)`) that partially mitigates the concrete overwrite outcome for those entities even though the transactional gap is real; the other 5 sites (trackConfig, learnerProfile, stageDefinition, profileProgram, settings) have no such backstop and are fully exposed to the described silent-overwrite failure. This does not change the verdict but the acceptance-criteria fault-injection test should target one of the unguarded 5 to reliably reproduce the failure.
